Your dedication and will to learn and teach are monumental compared to newer generations' attention spans. I speak for most who watch; you have made a historical impact on us. It seems that transnational capitalism, known as Franosism, has woven its web over hundreds of years, transforming into the monster it is today. What are humanity's possible counters? Do you think religion might be one? Will we ever make a cyclic turn away from capitalism? How long would it take to undo this movement?

Okay, so you're absolutely right. Thank you for this question.

The Franus has spent centuries preparing for today and that's why they win because they are willing to think long term, work together, and make necessary sacrifices to achieve heaven on earth in their eyes. If you want to defeat them, you need to become like that—think long term, understand the necessity of making sacrifices.

Okay? It’s something that cannot be defeated in one day or ten years or a hundred years; it requires belief in oneself and humanity. Respond by working hard, learning, and making sacrifices.

When empires come into being, they end because patcha becomes arrogant, narrow-minded, and insular. Pria will fall—how long it lasts is uncertain but highly unstable. So we need to look ahead and think about what humanity looks like after Pat Judea.

The world might be on the brink of significant changes. Wars and destruction are everywhere; perhaps 9% of humanity gets wiped out. We need to prepare for this and envision how we can rebuild together.

You speak a lot about the monad and gnostic teachings. Do you see this as a possible emerging major religion? Can it be? Societies rise and fall, much like the bronze age or the French revolution, creating opportunities for creativity and growth. Are societies who participate in collapse better off for it? Lastly, who are your favorite English language poets apart from Milton?

I was an English major at Yale, so I know about English poetry. My favorites include John Keats and William Shakespeare.

Societies rise and fall to allow new ones to emerge with creativity. Parents must die so that children can be independent; this is part of the human experience. We should see destruction and war not as negative but as inevitable parts of growth and rebirth. Even though there's stagnation, it means potential for renewal.
